correctness.rationale: The first-passage event is exactly equivalent to a Bernoulli random walk staying below the integer boundaries \(\lceil q_s(\beta)\rceil\). The derivative identity \(q_s'(\beta)=[s g(\beta)-\log(1/\alpha)]/(\beta^2\Delta)\), together with \(g'(\beta)=\beta\kappa''(\beta)>0\), proves that every relevant level equation has at most two roots. The packaged verifier then enumerates the resulting finite cells and computes the displayed example with exact rational dynamic programming. Risks: floating bisection is used only to locate isolated roots; the verifier checks residuals and root separation, while the probability arithmetic itself is exact.

value.rationale: The finding changes finite-horizon tuning of an actual sequential test: exact first-passage type-II error can have a broad plateau whose location differs materially from the smooth horizon stationary point. The theorem gives a finite exact reduction for every Bernoulli horizon, and the concrete design has a visible error reduction from about \(0.48157\) to \(0.45529\). The result is therefore a motivated structural boundary phenomenon rather than a routine recomputation of one binomial tail.
